messages.author: d42c7062482960a4
messages.subject: >10 day runtime in HPC for hierarchical Poisson model
parts:
I'm still running large, hierarchical models on an HPC, and one of them timed out after 10 days run time (with 1TB memory). I'm trying to find out why these models take so long, and what I can expect the total run time to be (apart from the large number of random effects). 

The log file has not changed for several days, and seems to be stuck on some heavy calculations. 

-Can anyone estimate how far this model was towards completion?
-Also, can anyone explain why a Poisson model takes much longer than the corresponding log transformed model (which took 6 days)?


Thanks
Roel

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] >10 day runtime in HPC for hierarchical Poisson model
parts:
If you have a HPC with 1TB of memory and enough time, I guess you can (i think the model got stuck at this point after only 2 days).
Other things you should know:
The data are quite spare, with lots of 0's, but models with smaller subsets of the data seem to run.
I use rather old R and INLA versions because the HPC people are unable or unwilling to update their systems. I tried running a recent INLA version but ran into a Linux  file not being up to date.

I'll send you the files in a few minutes
